questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: It was crucial to pick an English-speaking destination where I could also see myself in the culture, which is why Edinburgh was perfect. It also has a clear connection to English literature so it made perfect sense for me to go there

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: You get emails about everything so it is quite easy to figure out

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: Assistance is available if you need and you are told of your options

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: On campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
questions.answer: The distinction between off campus and on campus is a bit hard to make in Edinburgh as the whole city is basically one big campus with student accommodation scattered around the city, some closer to campus than others

questions.question: What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
questions.answer: There were catered or self-catered options available, in self-catered accommodation you share a kitchen with others. I shared with 4 others which made it feel like a roomie situation

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about on campus housing? *
questions.answer: It is quite expensive if you want to be close to everything in the city and if you want a bathroom for yourself

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: A lot of the buildings are old and are not isolated as great as it could be, so during the winter months it can get quite cold

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: It was a bit chaotic as it was uncertain which courses I could take so I ended up with some courses that I didn't really want or missed out on some that I wanted more. It is probably easier for other degrees though

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: It was different in my case as I was on a special agreement

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: You could email people at the university for help if you wanted but that was kind of it

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I ended up just applying for ten different courses and hoping I got just any of them, which was a bit sad as I also wanted some other courses that was outside of my special agreement

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: I'm not sure, hopefully it's a bit more clear in the future

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: It was different from home, but the professors were all very good.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA courses at your host university? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The level was pretty much the same as at home, though we spent less time on individual material which made the work load a bit heavier and didn't seem to go as much in depth as I am used to

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: The classes were much smaller which was a bit intimidating and you were more expected to be prepared for seminars. Answers also seemed more standardised than at home

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: Working Class Representations, Horror and Mystery, Ideology and Literature

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Working Class Representations turned out to be my favourite course, I found it very interesting and the professor was very welcoming and open to discussion

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: I expected the accommodation to provide pillows, duvets and kitchen stuff but the apartment was completely empty when i got there, so expect to buy everything from a pillow to pans, pots and cutlery

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Food was more expensive though it is almost the same as Copenhagen

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: There is a society for everything

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Everything, you could join any society you wanted, from sports to cultural societies to book clubs

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Get out of your comfort zone a bit, try some Scottish dancing or something like that. Also, take your chance to explore the city and the country

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Go to the Highlands and experience the country, it is magnificent

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Really easy as it is very similar to Denmark, the people are just more friendly

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Speaking with the Scottish students is really easy as they are typically very open, though a lot of the English students can be a bit harder to get close to

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: None

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The friendliness and the fact that they really cater to their culture and are proud to show it with honesty and humour

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Bring warm clothes if you are going for the autumn semester, try the local food, even if it is not great, socialise and meet people

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Enjoy your time and the city as there is really nothing like it

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Experiencing the culture and seeing the country which I have fallen a little bit in love with

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Sharing a kitchen with four others

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
